input.body:
label: bug
file: src/export/scheduler.ts

In `nextRunAt`, the "weekly" branch unconditionally advances the date by 7 days after setting the hour to `RUN_HOUR_UTC`, unlike the "daily" branch which only advances if the computed time has already passed. So if a weekly schedule is created earlier in the day than `RUN_HOUR_UTC` (e.g. 05:40 UTC, before the 06:00 UTC run time), the due run later that same day is skipped and the first export is pushed a full week out. This matches the reports: a schedule created at 09:00 (after 06:00) worked fine, while one created at 05:40 (before 06:00) missed its first Monday send.

input.title: Fix weekly schedules skipping their first run when created before 06:00 UTC
input.body:
File: src/export/scheduler.ts

In nextRunAt, the "weekly" branch unconditionally does next.setUTCDate(next.getUTCDate() + 7) after setting the hour to RUN_HOUR_UTC, unlike the "daily" branch which only advances a day if the computed time has already passed (next <= from). This means that when a weekly schedule is created earlier in the day than RUN_HOUR_UTC (06:00 UTC), the next run is pushed a full week ahead instead of running later that same day, silently skipping the first scheduled send. When created after 06:00 UTC, the unconditional +7 happens to match the intended "next week" behavior, which is why the August test (created at 09:00) appeared to work while the October one (created at 05:40) did not.

Proposed change: make the weekly (and monthly) branches use the same conditional advance as daily — only move forward by the cadence interval if the computed time (today at RUN_HOUR_UTC) is not strictly after `from`. That way a schedule created before RUN_HOUR_UTC on its first day fires that same day, and one created after RUN_HOUR_UTC correctly waits a full cadence interval.
